subject: Engineering Fundamentals
title: Limestone: Skeletons of Ancient Seas
description: A micro-lesson that makes Limestone: Skeletons of Ancient Seas usable.

hook.text: The Great Pyramid is mostly limestone. Each block is made of compressed seashells millions of years old.

buildup.text: Limestone forms when marine organisms die and settle on the ocean floor. Their calcium carbonate shells compress into rock.

discovery.text: Limestone is soft enough to carve with hand tools but hard enough to support massive structures.

twist.text: Acid rain dissolves limestone. Many medieval cathedrals are slowly melting away in polluted cities.

climax.text: Burn limestone and you get quickite — the key ingredient in cement. One stone launched two industries.

punchline.text: Ancient sea creatures built the pyramids.

quiz.question: What happens when limestone is burned at high temperatures?
options: It becomes glass that can be shaped into windows
It produces quicklime, the key ingredient in cement
It releases trapped fossils preserved inside the stone
